¿Cómo se calcula el punto muerto?: How is the break-even point calculated?
Q* = CF/(p − cv). Con costes fijos de 10: Q* = FC/(p − vc). With fixed costs of €10,000, price €25 and unit variable cost €15: Q* = 10,000/10 = 1000 units, with revenue of €25,000.
¿Cuánto hay que vender para un beneficio: How much must be sold for a target profit?
Q = (CF + B)/(p − cv). Para ganar 5000 €: Q = (FC + P)/(p − vc). To earn €5000 in the example: (10,000 + 5000)/10 = 1500 units.

Los costes fijos (alquiler, sueldos fijo: Fixed costs (rent, fixed salaries, insurance, depreciation) do not depend on what is sold; variable costs (raw materials, commissions, shipping) grow with each unit. Total costs are TC = FC + c<sub>v</sub> · Q and revenue, TR = p · Q.
Cada unidad vendida deja $m = p − c_v$ p: Each unit sold leaves $m = p − c_v$ to pay the fixed costs. The break-even point or profitability threshold is the quantity at which revenue and costs are equal and profit is 0:
Por debajo hay pérdidas y por encima, be: Below it there are losses and above it, profits: each extra unit adds m euros to profit.
El margen de seguridad, $(Q − Q^*)/Q$, d: The margin of safety, $(Q − Q^*)/Q$, says how far sales can fall before losing money. The degree of operating leverage, $DOL = {m · Q}/B$, says how many times a change in sales is amplified in profit: a company with many fixed costs has a high DOL, earns a lot when it sells and loses a lot when it does not.
Para ganar un beneficio B hay que vender: To earn a profit B you must sell $Q = (FC + B)/m$ units.
